h1: The 5 Best Kenmore Bagged Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Kenmore Bagged Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five Kenmore bagged vacuums, from the Elite upright to HEPA canisters and a hair-wrap upright, with real specs and tradeoffs.
summary: The Kenmore Elite 31150 is the best overall, a bagged upright with triple HEPA filtration, a beltless 3D Inducer motor and five height positions. The 400 Series canister is the complete kit for stairs and mixed floors, and the 200 Series is the cheapest route to HEPA. The Intuition upright cuts hair wrap, and the 600 Series is under-documented.
intro: Kenmore's range confuses buyers because uprights and canisters share naming conventions and series numbers, so a 200 Series and a 600 Series look like the same machine at different prices. They are not. The real choice is between an upright that attacks wall-to-wall carpet and a lightweight canister that carries easily up stairs and reaches under furniture. Filtration is the second split, since only some models state HEPA.

Our editors reviewed Kenmore's bagged models from their listed specifications: filtration, motor design, tools and reach. A bag is a plus for people who dislike emptying a dusty bin, because the dirt stays sealed. Models whose listings omit key specs lost points, since a name is not a feature, and a series number tells you little.

products.name: Kenmore Elite 31150 Pet Friendly Bagged Upright Beltless Vacuum
products.verdict: The most fully equipped Kenmore upright, with triple HEPA and no belt to replace.
products.description:
The Elite 31150 is a bagged upright with triple HEPA filtration, a beltless 3D Inducer motor, a telescoping wand and five height positions. Triple HEPA matters in a bagged machine because bag, filter and exhaust stages all trap fine dust, and the height settings match the brushroll to pile depth. No belt means one fewer wear part.

It takes the top spot by combining the strongest filtration with the least maintenance. Against the 400 Series canister it handles carpet better, but it is heavier to carry and clumsier on stairs.

Buy it for carpeted homes with pets or allergy sufferers. The caveats are weight on stairs and the $200 to $500 price. If you clean mostly bare floors or stairs, the canister is a better tool.
products.idealFor: Carpeted homes with pets and allergy concerns.
products.skipIf: You mostly clean bare floors or stairs.

products.name: Kenmore 81414 400 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum
products.verdict: A HEPA canister with an extended wand, retractable cord and four tools.
products.description:
The 81414 400 Series is a lightweight bagged canister with HEPA filtration, an extended telescoping wand, a retractable cord and four cleaning tools. A canister puts the motor in a separate body that you pull along, which keeps your arm light on stairs, curtains and under beds.

It ranks second because the kit is complete, but it has no upright brushroll width for big carpets, so a large rug takes more passes. Against the 200 Series it adds a retractable cord, an extra tool and an extended wand for the extra money.

Choose it for homes with stairs and mixed floors. Skip it if one machine must handle wall-to-wall carpet. The caveat: the body drags behind you, and on thick pile the head does less than an upright with a powered brushroll.
products.idealFor: Homes with stairs and mixed flooring.
products.skipIf: You want one machine for wall-to-wall carpet.

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum
products.verdict: The cheapest route to HEPA and a two-motor canister.
products.description:
The 81214 200 Series is a bagged canister with HEPA filtration, a 2 Motor System and three cleaning tools. The two motors split the work, one for suction and one for the powered head, which helps on mixed floors. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks third because it drops a tool and the extended wand of the 400 Series, in exchange for saving a price bracket. Against the Hair Eliminator upright, it gives you HEPA and a separate suction motor, which the Intuition does not list.

It fits budget shoppers who want HEPA and a light body for stairs and hard floors. The caveats are fewer accessories and no extended wand, so ceiling corners and tall shelves are out of reach. If you want more reach, pay for the 400 Series.
products.idealFor: Budget shoppers who want HEPA filtration.
products.skipIf: You need the longest reach or most tools.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum with Hair Eliminator Brushroll
products.verdict: An upright built to cut down on hair wrapping the brushroll.
products.description:
The Intuition is a bagged upright whose selling point is the Hair Eliminator brushroll. Long hair wraps around standard brushrolls and stalls them, which means stopping to cut strands free with scissors. A brushroll built to resist that saves chore time in a long-haired or shedding household.

It ranks fourth because it lacks HEPA and a canister's reach, and the listing gives few other specs. Compared with the Elite, it costs much less and offers far less equipment. It does solve one common irritation well.

It suits long-haired households on carpet that can accept standard filtration. Skip it if allergy-grade filtration matters most. The caveats are the thin spec sheet and the absence of HEPA, so ask the seller about filtration and the bag type before ordering.

products.name: Kenmore 600 Series Pet Friendly Bagged Canister Vacuum
products.verdict: Kenmore's top canister line, though the listing is short on detail.
products.description:
The 600 Series is a pet friendly bagged canister in the $200 to $500 bracket. The listing names the series and the pet friendly design, and little else, so the filtration, motor setup and tool count are not stated.

It ranks last because those unknowns are exactly what the 400 Series lists. Against that model, you pay for the series name more than for proven extras. The 400 Series states HEPA, a retractable cord and four tools in the same bracket.

It fits buyers loyal to the 600 Series line who accept that they are buying on reputation. Skip it if you want confirmed HEPA and a known tool count. Before ordering, ask the seller for the filtration type, motor details and bag number, and compare them with the 400 Series.
products.idealFor: Buyers loyal to the 600 Series line.
products.skipIf: You want confirmed HEPA and tool counts.

whatMatters.detail: HEPA filters capture very fine dust that standard filters let back into the room, which matters for allergies and pets. A bagged vacuum can still leak without one, because dust escapes at the exhaust. Look for the word HEPA in the title or bullets, not just allergen wording, and check whether the filter is replaceable and what it costs to replace.

Uprights clean carpet fast with a wide brushroll, while canisters are lighter in the hand and reach stairs, furniture and ceilings. Neither is better in the abstract. Match the style to your floors before comparing anything else, and think about stairs, since carrying an upright up a flight is a chore, and a canister struggles on deep carpet.

Belts stretch and break, then need a replacement and a quick repair that interrupts cleaning. A beltless design avoids that. Check the listing for beltless or 3D Inducer wording, which is how Kenmore names its belt-free drive. It also keeps the brushroll spinning at consistent speed as the machine ages, which keeps cleaning consistent.

Long hair wraps around a brushroll and can stall it, which means a pair of scissors and lost time. Brushrolls with a hair-cutting or anti-wrap feature cut that chore. Look for the Hair Eliminator or a similar name, and note that canisters with powered heads can face the same wrap problem. Cutting hair free takes time.

Tools and wands decide whether the vacuum cleans stairs, corners and furniture, not just open floor. A telescoping wand extends reach to ceilings and tall shelves. Check the number of tools and whether the wand telescopes. The 400 Series lists four tools, the 200 Series lists three, and the 600 Series states none.

faq.a: They hold suction better as the bag fills than many bagless models, but a very full bag does reduce airflow. Replace it before it is packed, and use the correct bag type. A full bag also lets dust back into the motor.

faq.q: Are any of these compatible with any bag?
faq.a: Kenmore uses specific bag types by model. Check the listing for the exact bag number before buying, because the wrong bag can leak dust and cut airflow. Stock a few spares so you do not run out.

faq.q: Is the Elite worth it over the 400 Series?
faq.a: Only if you have carpet. The 400 Series is lighter and better for stairs, and the 200 Series adds HEPA for less money. The Elite wins on carpet pile and pet hair.

Attach the wand and tools and fit the bag. Most models need no tools, but read the manual for the correct order, and check that the bag is seated before switching on. A badly fitted bag leaks dust straight into the motor.

faq.q: How do I maintain HEPA filters?
faq.a: Replace them on the schedule in the manual, and never wash a paper HEPA unless it says so. A damp filter can grow mould and lose its ability to trap fine dust. Keep a spare if the manual allows.
Canisters with a floor tool are gentler on hardwood. On the Elite, use the height setting to match the pile so it does not scatter debris. Move slowly over loose grit on bare boards.

finalTake: Buy the Elite 31150 for carpeted homes with pets, and the 400 Series canister if stairs and hard floors dominate. The 200 Series is the budget HEPA choice, the Intuition suits long-haired households, and the 600 Series is worth buying only once the seller confirms its filtration and tools.
